bugs: Later cleanup failures overwrite first IO/Memory cause or pending destructor business error; path-copy failure still formats
Windows finished process with real exit259 is misread as STILL_ACTIVE
POSIX contender locks already-unlinked inode after original holder release and path replacement; same-path reentry also misses identity

implementation.errorHandling: Take/restore existing XRT error owner without new wrapper diagnostic; finish delete/unlock/close even after failure. Public methods clear old error, destroy preserves business cause.
implementation.identity: XRT FileStat/PathStat Available/Device/Identity; query failure preserved, missing identity Unsupported, mismatch State. No hidden retry/reopen.
implementation.liveness: WaitForSingleObject(process,0), close local process handle; preserve conservative access-denied behavior
implementation.posix: Declare _POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L before package system headers for strict C11 kill declaration
implementation.cost: Two metadata queries for fresh successful lock and same-path reentry; Windows actual OOM sweep gains one failure point. No new cache or body copy; no zero-overhead or throughput claim.

cleanup.kernelFileCalls: Normal open/locks/delete/close are real. Close hook retires real native file before reporting failure. POSIX unlock errors arise from errno path, not a forged XRT API result.
cleanup.guards: No-allocation guard starts after precreated cause; not a claim that every POSIX errno-to-XRT initial diagnostic allocates zero bytes

liveness.handleMeasurement: Immediately before/after isAlive only, not unrelated process/CRT initialization

identity.schedule: Real fd opened by contender; hook invokes original owner release and replacement owner write before real flock; no fabricated file identity or successful lock
identity.samePathReentry: Rename held inode, replacement owns original path, stale reentry rejected; stale release does not delete replacement; explicit retry succeeds

oldBaseline.comparison: Same final fixtures, only core include mechanically redirected to saved original source
